lines.text: It’s project time! Build a five-question quiz game on a topic you love.
Start with score = 0 before the first question.
Each time the player is right, add one with score += 1.
At the end, the variable holds the total.
Each question is an input() followed by an if and an else.
The if gives the point and says Correct.
The else kindly shows the right answer.
Players type in different ways. answer.lower() makes the answer small letters, and .strip() removes extra spaces.
Then one comparison catches them all.
After the last question, use if, elif and else on the score.
Five gets Quiz Champion, three or more gets Star Player, and so on.
The score starts at zero, like a fresh scoreboard before a match.
Both lines add one, and plus equals is just a shorter way to write it.
The player typed MARS in capitals with an extra space.
strip and lower clean it up to mars, so the answer still counts.
With a score of four, the first test is False, but the elif is True.
Always put the biggest score first, or everyone becomes a Star Player.
Good coders plan before they type. Write your questions on paper first.
Build one question, test it, then copy the pattern for the rest.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
